title: The revocation appended a suffix to the holder's assignment identifier for its end command, so a valid 128-character assignment identifier made the command identifier invalid and failed the whole revoke transaction
resolution: The end command identifier comes from the port RevocationCommandIds, a deterministic derivation that must be bounded; B derives it as a SHA-256 digest. A test with the longest assignment identifier fails before the fix with invalid.

title: The grace age does not stop the sweep from discarding the version of an add-slot command delayed past it between its store and its add commit, so the record could name a discarded version
resolution: Coordinator decision M2: the add measures, on an injected monotonic clock, the time from before its store to the end of its add transaction; past half the least grace age it rolls back, discards its version, and fails with unavailable. A test with an injected clock fails before it.

title: The rotation interleavings that contract section 9 requires were untested: two rotations reading one revision, a later switch before an earlier cleanup, and a higher orphan removed by the next rotation
resolution: In-memory tests with one-shot hooks cover another rotation between store and switch, a switch before an earlier cleanup, and a higher orphan; PostgreSQL tests gate two switches after their held count read and assert the loser's retry and conflict; three mutants fail them.

title: No test removed a reserved active slot to show the credential destroyed, no cancellation command, the reservation kept until the terminal fact, and the re-delivery refused
resolution: A PostgreSQL test removes the slot of a launched attempt with an earlier delivery, checks each effect, refuses the re-delivery with removed, and releases the reservation at the drain; two mutants fail it.

title: The held-for-credential read used an any-element test that the partial GIN index on the credential column cannot serve, while the design called its sequential scan unavoidable
resolution: The read uses the containment test that the capacity ledger already uses, which the index serves, and the design risk now says so. A plan comparison on a throwaway database shows an index condition only for the new test.

title: A revocation left a running holder's assignment in its state while contract section 8.1 said the revocation cancels the assignment, and no test asserted that state
resolution: Contract section 8.1 and design decision 3 now say the assignment keeps its state and held reservation until the terminal fact ends it, because ending it now would refuse a re-delivery with assignment-not-active; the PostgreSQL test asserts the state, and a mutant that ends it fails.

title: A credential call that rejected for one slot rejected the whole sweep and skipped every later slot
resolution: Each slot's work is settled on its own, and the sweep answers the swept and the failed slots; a test with one unreachable slot fails before the fix.

title: An update naming the stored allowed projects in another order advanced the revision, against the decision that a repeat changes nothing
resolution: The settings compare the allowed projects as sorted lists; a test with the projects reordered fails before the fix.

title: The revocation command id derivation had a plural type name, and the sweep answered an unnamed count that included slots where nothing was discarded
resolution: The type is RevocationCommandIdFor, and the sweep answers a named result with its swept and failed slots.

title: Contract section 6.2 said the listed pairs close the add race, while the record admitted they close it only within the grace age
resolution: With the coordinator's decision M2 the section says the pairs close the race for any add that commits within half the grace age and that a slower add aborts, which the add deadline guard enforces.
